A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learning Color Equivariant Representations. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification experiments, sample-efficiency and equivariance analyses, and Caltech-101 segmentation results in Appendix E.3.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including classification Tables 1–6 and segmentation results in Appendix F.3 and Table 8.

M1.justification: Equation (15) revises the stated convolution layer: the channel sum changes from K^0 to K^l and the filter argument from g^{-1}h to h^{-1}g, matching Equation (2). This is a limited correction to the method specification; the architecture, lifting procedure and training objectives are retained, with no demonstrated implementation change.

E1.justification: The classification datasets and global/local hue, saturation and luminance scenarios are retained, as are CIFAR-10 color sorting and Caltech-101 segmentation. The additional experiments in v6 Appendix F already appeared in v4 Appendix E.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Z2CNN, CEConv-3/4, ResNet, grayscale and color-augmentation variants, and conventional segmentation baseline. The added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their splits, preprocessing, metrics, parameter counts and training budgets. The experimental settings in v4 Appendices C–E are preserved in v6 Appendices D–F.

E4.justification: The sample-efficiency sweep, hue-discretization/invertibility analysis, equivariance-error comparison, feature-map visualizations, color sorting and hospital saturation statistics are retained. The appendix CEConv analyses are reordered without adding a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three seeds for Hue-shift MNIST, Hue-shift 3D Shapes and CIFAR-10, five for Camelyon17, and one for ImageNet, with identical seed values. Parenthesized table statistics and graphical uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 6 retains ImageNet errors of 30.66, 30.28 and 30.71 for ResNet18, Hue-3 and CEConv-3; segmentation errors remain 11.25 for Conv and 9.67 for Hue-3, moving from Table 7 to Table 8.

T1.justification: New Appendix A explicitly constructs the hue and saturation sets and operations and supplies derivations for closure, associativity, identity and inverses. This substantially expands the formal treatment beyond v4's identification with known groups and group-action arguments. The existing action proofs move to Appendix B, with the hue proof expressed modulo 2π instead of 255.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about input-image lifting, avoiding invalid RGB rotations, reducing equivariance error by over three orders of magnitude, extending equivariance to saturation and luminance, and improving generalization and sample efficiency.

C2.justification: The explanations based on structured representations and CEConv's equivariance errors are retained. Section 6 preserves the computational-cost and finite-group approximation limitations and the proposed investigation of continuous representations.

D1.justification: The reported code URL, dataset access instructions, hardware and per-experiment hyperparameters are unchanged. The segmentation backbone specification is retained as v6 Table 7, previously v4 Table 8.

R1.justification: v6 adds introductory citations and references to Esteves et al.'s spherical CNN work and Zhong and Allen-Blanchette's GaGrasp. The substantive positioning against CEConv and color-invariance approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 inserts the group-proof appendix, updates cross-references and places the CEConv feature-map subsection before color sorting. Existing prose receives limited edits, including introductory wording and an added acknowledgment; the main narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: Both versions retain 20 figures and eight tables. Appendix figures are regrouped and renumbered, including feature-map Figures 13–14 becoming Figures 9–10, while the segmentation backbone and results tables exchange numbers and are placed together. The visual designs and displayed experimental content remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 improves the consistency of Equation (15) and makes the group constructions explicit. However, the new hue-group proof drops the necessary outer modulus in Equation (32), and its inverse formula gives 2π for the identity although the defined set excludes 2π. These introduced proof defects undermine the intended rigor benefit; with empirical support unchanged, the balance between clarification and mathematical reliability does not establish a reliable net quality direction.
